chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, who said:

An prisoner was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) on the day of Siffin, so he gave him bay'ah (pledge of security). Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'I will not kill you, for I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.' So he released him and gave him the spoils he had brought with him.

key_terms.بَايَعَهُ: He gave him bay'ah (pledge of security/guarantee)
key_terms.صِفِّينَ: Siffin, the location of the battle between Ali and Muawiyah

ai.seo_question: What did Ali (peace be upon him) do with a prisoner from the Battle of Siffin regarding killing and spoils?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) demonstrates the principle of *bay'ah* (pledge of security) by granting safety to a Kufah prisoner at Siffin, prioritizing divine accountability over immediate military advantage. His declaration, 'I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds,' underscores the theological basis for clemency in warfare, while returning the prisoner's spoils highlights the ethical treatment of captives beyond mere survival. This incident is frequently cited by Shia jurists to establish the validity of unilateral security grants by the Imam or commander.
